findings.reason: the §9 build node implementing the named predicate literally satisfies the wrong rule and fails §9's first done-when case, so the predicate (or §3's docstring) must be corrected before dispatch.
findings.text: §9 says a whole-plan dependency is satisfied "when at least one of its sections is done and none is left implementable, read through §3's open-section predicate", but that predicate, `open_sections` (reckon/_plan_html.py:869-882), returns `implementable` OR `deferred`, and its own docstring says "roadmap readiness reads the same list to decide whether a whole-plan dependency is satisfied" — a roadmap implementing `not open_sections(target)` blocks a target of {s1 done, s2 deferred}, which §9's own done-when (line 175) requires to be *ready*

findings.reason: without the reader named, the §9 node has no declared way to detect the case its own done-when tests, so it may ship the undeclared-heading branch never firing.
findings.text: §9 requires the roadmap to report `undeclared-heading` for "a plan with an authored heading that carries no declaration", but §9 names `open_sections` (which reads the declaration map, so a heading absent from it is invisible) and the `sections` records reachable through `_plan_authored_state` (built from `data-reckon="section"` elements, which an undeclared heading does not have) as the only readers; the detector that does see such a heading is §3's `derive_section_todos`/`authored_section_headings`, which §9 never names

findings.reason: a reader resolving whole-plan readiness from the older rationale implements the clearing rule and satisfies a dependency §9's done-when requires held, so the older rationale must be amended to match the locked 2026-10-08 decision.
findings.text: the locked decision `deferred-counts-as-ticked` states "a whole-plan dependency clears once no section is left implementable", which clears an all-deferred target (no section is implementable), while §9 (line 174) and the newer `uncertain-dependency` rationale (line 195) hold that same all-deferred target blocked as `deferred-only` — the decisions block states two opposite rules for the one uncertain case
